cards.back: A rock formed when magma or lava cools and hardens. Granite and basalt are igneous.
cards.say: igneous rock. A rock formed when magma or lava cools and hardens. Granite and basalt are igneous.

cards.back: A rock formed from layers of sediment pressed together. Sandstone and limestone are sedimentary.
cards.say: sedimentary rock. A rock formed from layers of sediment pressed together. Sandstone and limestone are sedimentary.

cards.back: A rock changed by great heat and pressure. Marble is made from limestone.
cards.say: metamorphic rock. A rock changed by great heat and pressure. Marble is made from limestone.

cards.front: Which type of rock is marble?
cards.back: Metamorphic.
cards.say: Which type of rock is marble? Metamorphic.

cards.front: Which type of rock is granite?
cards.back: Igneous.
cards.say: Which type of rock is granite? Igneous.

cards.front: Which type of rock is sandstone?
cards.back: Sedimentary.
cards.say: Which type of rock is sandstone? Sedimentary.

cards.back: The way rocks slowly change from one type to another over millions of years.
cards.say: rock cycle. The way rocks slowly change from one type to another over millions of years.

cards.back: The breaking down of rock into smaller pieces by rain, wind, ice and heat.
cards.say: weathering. The breaking down of rock into smaller pieces by rain, wind, ice and heat.

cards.back: When weathered pieces of rock are carried away by water, wind or ice.
cards.say: erosion. When weathered pieces of rock are carried away by water, wind or ice.

cards.back: Small pieces of rock, sand and mud that settle in layers.
cards.say: sediment. Small pieces of rock, sand and mud that settle in layers.

cards.back: Sediment settles in layers, is buried and pressed together until it becomes rock.
cards.say: How does sedimentary rock form? Sediment settles in layers, is buried and pressed together until it becomes rock.

cards.back: The remains or traces of a dead living thing that has been preserved in rock.
cards.say: fossil. The remains or traces of a dead living thing that has been preserved in rock.

cards.front: In which kind of rock are fossils found?
cards.back: Mostly sedimentary rock.
cards.say: In which kind of rock are fossils found? Mostly sedimentary rock.

cards.back: A dead organism is buried in sediment. Over millions of years its hard parts are replaced by minerals and the sediment turns into rock.
cards.say: How does a fossil form? A dead organism is buried in sediment. Over millions of years its hard parts are replaced by minerals and the sediment turns into rock.

cards.back: What kinds of life existed in the past and how living things have changed.
cards.say: What can fossils tell us? What kinds of life existed in the past and how living things have changed.

cards.back: Allowing water to pass through. Sandstone is permeable.
cards.say: permeable. Allowing water to pass through. Sandstone is permeable.

cards.back: A mixture of tiny pieces of rock, humus, water, air and living things.
cards.say: soil. A mixture of tiny pieces of rock, humus, water, air and living things.

cards.back: Rotted plant and animal material in soil. It adds nutrients.
cards.say: humus. Rotted plant and animal material in soil. It adds nutrients.

cards.back: The top layer of soil, rich in humus. Most plant roots grow here.
cards.say: topsoil. The top layer of soil, rich in humus. Most plant roots grow here.

cards.front: Which soil drains water fastest: sandy or clay?
cards.back: Sandy soil. Its particles are big with large gaps.
cards.say: Which soil drains water fastest: sandy or clay? Sandy soil. Its particles are big with large gaps.

cards.front: Which soil holds the most water?
cards.back: Clay. Its particles are tiny and packed closely.
cards.say: Which soil holds the most water? Clay. Its particles are tiny and packed closely.

cards.front: Why are earthworms good for soil?
cards.back: Their tunnels let air and water in and they mix in rotting plant material.
cards.say: Why are earthworms good for soil? Their tunnels let air and water in and they mix in rotting plant material.

cards.back: Soil being washed or blown away. Cutting down trees makes it worse.
cards.say: soil erosion. Soil being washed or blown away. Cutting down trees makes it worse.

cards.front: How can adding compost help soil?
cards.back: It adds humus and nutrients and helps the soil hold water.
cards.say: How can adding compost help soil? It adds humus and nutrients and helps the soil hold water.

cards.front: Why is volcanic soil often very fertile?
cards.back: It is rich in minerals from volcanic rock.
cards.say: Why is volcanic soil often very fertile? It is rich in minerals from volcanic rock.
